parts.visual:
Your personal brand is what people say about you when you leave the room. In the executive world, a strong brand opens doors before you even knock.

Elements of a Brand:
1. Consistency: Doing what you say you will do, every time.
2. Niche Expertise: Being the undeniable 'go-to' person for a specific topic.
3. Visibility: Sharing insights publicly (LinkedIn, panels, internal meetings).
parts.audio: Your personal brand is what people say about you when you leave the room. Build it through consistency, niche expertise, and visibility.

questions.question: Which of these is the most effective way to build a personal brand internally at a company?
options: Bragging about your IQ to everyone.
Consistently volunteering to solve complex, cross-departmental problems.
questions.correct_answer: Consistently volunteering to solve complex, cross-departmental problems.
questions.explanation: A brand is built on action and value delivery, not just appearance.

questions.question: Listen to the phrase. What element of personal branding is this?
questions.tts_text: I'm going to publish an article on LinkedIn summarizing our team's approach to AI integration.
questions.explanation: Doing great work is only half the battle. If nobody knows you did it, your brand cannot grow. Thought leadership creates visibility.

questions.question: Why is 'Niche Expertise' important for an executive's brand?
options: It isn't; you should know everything about everything.
Being known as 'The Turnaround Specialist' or 'The Data Privacy Expert' makes you highly memorable and sought after for specific high-level roles.
It makes you sound smart at parties.
questions.correct_answer: Being known as 'The Turnaround Specialist' or 'The Data Privacy Expert' makes you highly memorable and sought after for specific high-level roles.
questions.explanation: Generalists are useful, but specialists are remembered and recruited.

questions.question: What destroys an executive's personal brand the fastest?
options: A lack of integrity; failing to deliver on a major promise.
questions.correct_answer: A lack of integrity; failing to deliver on a major promise.
questions.explanation: Trust is the foundation of any brand. One major lie or broken promise can destroy years of reputation building.
